metadata.name: IRS CP91 Final Notice — Levy on Social Security Benefits Response
metadata.description: Respond to IRS CP91, the final notice before levy of up to 15% of Social Security benefits. Covers the Collection Due Process hearing, hardship relief, and collection alternatives.

verified.note: Confirmed as the final notice before levy on Social Security benefits. Carries a 30-day CDP window.

extraction.description: Extract identifying details and the notice-specific figures from a CP91.

fields.name: taxpayerName
fields.prompt: Extract the full taxpayer name from the notice header, exactly as printed.
fields.notes: On a joint return both names appear; capture the primary filer first.

fields.name: ssn
fields.prompt: Extract the Social Security Number or ITIN. Format XXX-XX-XXXX. If only the last four digits are shown, return what is shown.
fields.notes: If truncated, the full number must come from the taxpayer, never inferred.

fields.name: taxYear
fields.prompt: Extract the tax period this notice concerns. Return the 4-digit year.

fields.name: noticeDate
fields.prompt: Extract the notice date from the top right. Format YYYY-MM-DD.
fields.notes: Statutory periods run from this date, not from receipt.

fields.name: responseDeadline
fields.prompt: Extract the date by which the taxpayer must respond to prevent the levy — 30 days from the notice date. Format YYYY-MM-DD.
fields.notes: The 30-day CDP window. After it, only an Equivalent Hearing remains, which carries no Tax Court review.

fields.name: serviceCenter
fields.prompt: Extract the IRS office or service center that issued the notice, from the return address block.
fields.notes: Determines where the response is mailed. Never guess this.

fields.name: totalBalance
fields.prompt: Extract the total unpaid balance the levy would collect against.
fields.notes: Drives which collection alternatives are realistic.

fields.name: monthlyBenefitAmount
fields.prompt: Extract the monthly Social Security benefit amount if the notice states it.
fields.notes: 15% of this is what the levy takes each month; needed to show hardship.

fields.name: levyPercentage
fields.prompt: Extract the percentage of the benefit the IRS states it will levy. Usually 15.
fields.notes: The continuous levy under IRC 6331(h) is capped at 15% of the benefit.

extraction.notes: Where stated figures do not reconcile, re-read the later pages before proceeding.

validation.description: Validate that the CP91 response preserves the taxpayer's rights and commits to a concrete path.

rules.name: cdpDeadlineCompliance
rules.message: Request the Collection Due Process hearing within 30 days. After that only an Equivalent Hearing remains, with no Tax Court review.

rules.name: cdpRightsAsserted
rules.message: Request the Collection Due Process hearing in terms and file Form 12153. Describing the hardship is not a request.
rules.example_fail: A letter explaining that the levy would cause hardship.
rules.example_pass: A letter requesting a CDP hearing under IRC 6330 with Form 12153 enclosed.

rules.name: hardshipDocumented
rules.check: if hardship claimed: specific facts and evidence
rules.message: A levy on a fixed benefit is judged on the household budget. State monthly income and necessary expenses, with evidence.
rules.example_fail: The levy would be a hardship.
rules.example_pass: Monthly benefit $1,640 against rent $900, medications $210 and utilities $180, documented in the enclosed statements and Form 433-F.

rules.name: paymentOptionProvided
rules.message: Propose a collection alternative — currently not collectible status, an installment agreement, or an offer.
rules.example_fail: Asking only that the levy stop.
rules.example_pass: Requesting currently not collectible status with Form 433-F enclosed.

rules.name: noLiabilityAdmission
rules.message: Explain the circumstances without conceding the liability or fault.
rules.example_fail: We know we should have paid this years ago.
rules.example_pass: The enclosed Form 433-F shows monthly necessary expenses exceeding monthly income.

rules.name: correctAddressing
rules.check: addressed to issuing center with SSN and tax year
rules.message: Address the response to the issuing service center and reference your SSN and tax year so it is matched to the account.
rules.example_fail: Sent to a general IRS address with no account reference.

rules.name: professionalFormat
rules.message: Use a formal business letter with a proper address, date and signature.
rules.example_fail: A handwritten note on the notice stub.
rules.example_pass: A typed, dated and signed letter.

validation.notes: The costliest failure is a letter that reads as a response but exercises no right.

aiPrompt.system: You are a tax correspondence specialist experienced in Collection Due Process and levies on fixed income. You understand that a levy on Social Security strikes a household with no capacity to absorb it, and that the case is made on a documented budget rather than on sentiment.
aiPrompt.task: Prepare a Collection Due Process hearing request that both preserves the appeal right and makes the substantive case. Where the benefit is the household's primary income, build a documented budget showing that the levy would leave necessary living expenses unmet, and request currently not collectible status or an affordable alternative on that basis.
aiPrompt.format: Professional business letter addressed to the issuing IRS service center.
constraints: Request the CDP hearing in terms; describing hardship is not a request
Make the hardship case with figures — monthly income against itemised necessary expenses
Enclose Form 433-F or 433-A where hardship or an alternative is sought
Propose a specific alternative rather than asking only that the levy stop
Do not concede the liability while contesting the collection method
Cite only documents the taxpayer actually has
State facts and enclose proof; do not argue what the law requires

examples.output:
We request a Collection Due Process hearing under IRC 6330 for the periods shown. Form 12153 is enclosed.

Social Security is the sole household income, at $1,640.00 per month. Necessary monthly expenses are $900.00 rent, $210.00 prescription medications and $180.00 utilities, totalling $1,290.00 and documented in the enclosed lease, pharmacy statement and Form 433-F. A levy of 15%, or $246.00 per month, would leave $104.00 against all remaining necessities.

On that basis we request that the account be placed in currently not collectible status. This request is not an acknowledgement that the balance is correct.

aiPrompt.notes: Exercising the right explicitly costs nothing; omitting it forfeits something that cannot be recovered.

responseTemplate.description: Business letter responding to a CP91 notice.

sections.name: header
sections.template:
[IRS Service Center Address]

RE: CP91 Notice Response
Tax Year [Tax Year]
SSN: [SSN]
Notice Date: [Notice Date]

[Taxpayer Name]
[Taxpayer Address]

[Date]
sections.guidance: Address to the issuing service center. The RE: block is how the IRS matches the letter to the account.
sections.example:
Internal Revenue Service
Kansas City, MO 64999-0052

RE: CP91 Notice Response
Tax Year 2024
SSN: 123-45-6789
Notice Date: June 2, 2025

John Michael Smith
412 Oak Street
Springfield, MO 65807

June 16, 2025

sections.name: introduction
sections.template:
Dear Sir or Madam:

We are writing in response to your CP91 notice dated [Notice Date] regarding tax year [Tax Year].
sections.guidance: One sentence identifying the notice being answered.
sections.example:
Dear Sir or Madam:

We are writing in response to your CP91 notice dated June 2, 2025 regarding tax year 2024.

sections.name: itemByItemResponse
sections.guidance: Set out monthly income against itemised necessary expenses, then request the alternative that follows from those figures.
sections.example: Social Security is the sole household income at $1,640.00 per month against $1,290.00 of documented necessary expenses. A 15% levy would leave $104.00 for all remaining necessities.

sections.name: cdpRequest
sections.template: We request a Collection Due Process hearing under IRC 6330 for tax year [Tax Year]. Form 12153 is enclosed.
sections.guidance: Include whenever the CDP right is being exercised. The request must be explicit — describing the dispute is not a request.
sections.example: We request a Collection Due Process hearing under IRC 6330 for tax year 2024. Form 12153 is enclosed.

sections.name: conclusion
sections.template: Please confirm receipt of this response and update the account accordingly.
sections.guidance: Short close requesting confirmation and account update.
sections.example: Please confirm receipt of this response and update the account accordingly.

sections.name: signature
sections.template:
Sincerely,

[Taxpayer Name]
SSN: [SSN]

Enclosures:
[List of Attached Documents]
sections.guidance: Sign and list every enclosure so the IRS can confirm nothing is missing.
sections.example:
Sincerely,

John Michael Smith
SSN: 123-45-6789

Enclosures:
- Form 12153 Request for a Collection Due Process Hearing

legalFramework.description: Respond to IRS CP91, the final notice before levy of up to 15% of Social Security benefits. Covers the Collection Due Process hearing, hardship relief, and collection alternatives.
authorities: IRC 6330 — Notice and opportunity for hearing before levy
IRC 6331(h) — Continuous levy on specified payments, limited to 15%
IRC 6343(a)(1)(D) — Release of levy causing economic hardship
Form 12153 — Request for a Collection Due Process or Equivalent Hearing
precedents: A timely CDP request suspends the levy while the hearing is pending
The 15% continuous levy applies to the benefit until the liability is resolved or the levy is released
Economic hardship requires the levy to leave the taxpayer unable to meet basic living expenses
Currently not collectible status suspends collection without extinguishing the liability
A late request may proceed as an Equivalent Hearing, which carries no right of Tax Court review
criticalRules: Request the CDP hearing within 30 days and file Form 12153. This is the only step that suspends the levy.
Describing the hardship is not requesting a hearing. The request must be explicit or the right lapses.
Make the hardship case with figures. A documented budget showing necessary expenses exceeding income is what supports release; a description of difficulty is not.
Enclose Form 433-F. A hardship claim without a financial statement cannot be evaluated.
Contesting the levy is not conceding the liability, and the letter should say so.
A levy on Social Security is continuous — it recurs every month until released, so the window matters more here than on a one-time levy.

jurisdictionVariations.variation: Procedure is uniform nationwide under the Internal Revenue Code.
Deadlines may be postponed under IRC 7508A in federally declared disaster areas. Check current IRS relief for the taxpayer's county before treating a window as closed.

testCases.description: Cover the ordinary path and the edge cases for CP91.

cases.name: cp91-hardship-cnc
cases.description: Social Security is the sole income and a levy would leave expenses unmet
cases.inputDocument: CP91 with a $8,730.00 balance against a $1,640.00 monthly benefit
cases.expectedResponse: CDP hearing request with Form 12153, a documented budget, and a request for currently not collectible status.
successCriteria: Budget stated with figures and supporting documents

cases.name: cp91-window-closed
cases.description: Edge case: the notice is 40 days old
cases.inputDocument: CP91 dated 40 days before the response date
cases.expectedValidation: error — the 30-day CDP window has closed
cases.expectedResponse: Response explaining that only an Equivalent Hearing remains, which carries no Tax Court review, and pursuing hardship release under IRC 6343 in parallel.
successCriteria: The expired window is surfaced before mailing
The Equivalent Hearing limitation is explained
A levy release request under IRC 6343 is pursued as the substantive route

relatedWorkflows.description: CP91 in the collection and compliance sequence.
downstream: form-433-a — financial statement supporting hardship or an alternative
alternatives: form-656 — offer in compromise where the balance is permanently unpayable

implementation.notes: Highest-stakes notice in the collection sequence for fixed-income taxpayers. The levy is continuous, so every month of delay is a further 15% taken.
knownChallenges: Building a credible budget from what the taxpayer can document
Ensuring the CDP request is explicit rather than implied by the hardship narrative
Explaining that currently not collectible status suspends rather than cancels the liability
